title: Online task adaptation in Mirror-code space for cellular automata
hypothesis: For online adaptation of 1D binary cellular-automaton local transition rules, updating a two-coordinate Mirror code over a shared rule basis will reach the target rule with fewer update-state bytes than full-rule adaptation and preserve prior tasks when codes are banked. A hard task with rule logits outside the shared rank-2 subspace should expose the boundary where private/full-rule state is necessary.
physical_object: shared 8-entry local CA rule-logit vector plus rank-2 view basis
mirror_coordinate: per-task 2D code updated online from neighborhood/next-state observations
logical_multiplicity: multiple task-specific CA transition rules on one shared physical rule
controls: frozen shared rule without task adaptation
Mirror 2D code online SGD and per-task code bank
full 8-logit local-rule online SGD with per-task rule snapshots
independent per-task full rule state as quality/storage upper control
task: Predict next cell from one of 8 binary neighborhoods sampled from seeded 1D CA trajectories; report next-state accuracy by online examples, rule-logit MSE, retention of earlier tasks, inference bytes and update compute.

development.selection_metric: accuracy vs online examples and actual bytes on four development rules; no audit-driven code-rank changes

fresh.split: four development task rules estimate shared rank-2 basis; each fresh world contains four in-subspace rules and four independent hard rules, each with 256 online observations and 512 held-out observations

paid_objects: task code bank or full rule snapshots

success_gate: On >=2/3 fresh worlds, easy-rule Mirror accuracy after 64 online examples is within 5 percentage points of task-specific full-rule control and serialized code-bank payload <=60% of full-rule snapshots; previous-task accuracy after adapting all tasks remains >=95% of its post-adaptation value. Report hard-rule gap and update latency.
failure_gate: FAIL if easy-rule accuracy/storage/retention gate fails on >=2/3 seeds or if the hard-rule gap cannot be reduced by full local-rule state. PROMISING only when the easy-rule storage/quality/retention gates pass; no general CA claim.
boundaries: local rule prediction screen, not full spatial pattern-generation benchmark
logical task multiplicity is measured by held-out rule quality and bytes, not code combinations
no natural data or learned autonomous self-organization claim
